source.text: Nec mora praeceptis, cum protinus utraque virgo arcano egressae thalamo: mirabile visu, Pallados armisonae pharetrataeque ora Dianae aequa ferunt, terrore minus, nova deinde pudori visa virum facies: pariter pallorque ruborque purpureas hausere genas, oculique verentes ad sanctum rediere patrem, postquam ordine mensae victa fames, signis perfectam auroque nitentem Iasides pateram famulos ex more poposcit, qua Danaus libare deis seniorque Phoroncus assueti, tenet haec operum caelata figuras:
source.text_original: Nec mora praeceptis, cum protinus utraque virgo / arcano egressae thalamo: mirabile visu, / Pallados armisonae pharetrataeque ora Dianae / aequa ferunt, terrore minus, nova deinde pudori / visa virum facies: pariter pallorque ruborque / purpureas hausere genas, oculique verentes / ad sanctum rediere patrem, postquam ordine mensae / victa fames, signis perfectam auroque nitentem / Iasides pateram famulos ex more poposcit, / qua Danaus libare deis seniorque Phoroncus / assueti, tenet haec operum caelata figuras: /
source.text_english: Without delay, at the command, both maidens at once came forth from the hidden chamber: marvelous to behold, they bear faces like Pallas, battle-voiced, and like arrow-bearing Diana, with less of terror; then a man’s appearance seemed strange to their modesty. For both pallor and blush alike spread over their purple cheeks, and their eyes, in reverent fear, turned back to their holy father, after hunger had been conquered in due order at table. Then Iasides, when hunger had been satisfied, asked his servants for a goblet, complete with emblems and gleaming with gold, as was his custom, with which aged Danaus and old Phoroncus used to pour libations to the gods. This bears on it in embossed work the figures of exploits:

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: an socia Iunone et Pallade fretus armisona superet magis et freta iussa capessat, siqua operis tanti domito consurgere ponto fama queat?
reuse.text_original: an socia Iunone et Pallade fretus / armisona superet magis et freta iussa capessat, / siqua operis tanti domito consurgere ponto / fama queat?
reuse.text_english: Or, trusting in the aid of Juno and Pallas and in his warlike arms, might he more readily prevail and take up the appointed seas, if any fame of so great a deed can rise from the conquered deep?
